environment.note: Additive, value-blind, DARK correction to the ADR-0113 operator OAuth-health classifier (ADR-0118). A member who deliberately disconnects a Gmail mailbox (ConnectedMailbox.status=REVOKED, written ONLY by the owner's own MailboxRevokeView, which also deletes the credential) was classified RECONSENT_REQUIRED -> CRITICAL operator alert + MISCONFIGURED subsystem fault, inverting the module's purpose. The fix adds an eighth truthful status OWNER_DISCONNECTED (SEV_OK, recovery_required=False, no alert), keeps ERROR + REAUTH_CODES as RECONSENT_REQUIRED (the genuine 7-day-expiry case), maps OWNER_DISCONNECTED -> HealthState.HEALTHY in probe_mailbox_ingest (never a fault), adds owner_disconnected_count to the aggregate, surfaces it in the broker_mailbox_health CLI summary (so the summary reconciles) and renders the status distinctly (non-alert colour) on the DARK operator page. A migration-free defensive comment at the ConnectedMailbox.Status.REVOKED enum records the load-bearing invariant (REVOKED is member-initiated only; a future grant-death-as-REVOKED writer must revisit the classification). No migration, no model field change, no schedule, no flag enablement, no owner-facing banner change, no production/host/mailbox/withdrawal mutation. Latent in production today (operator probe + endpoint flags OFF); fixed before the operator-health path is armed. The owner-facing read-model (health.mailbox_health / customer_mailbox_status) and the pre-pkt-149 R1 CLI exit gates (--exit-nonzero-on-recovery/-degraded, which read it) are intentionally unchanged (a disconnected mailbox is truthfully 'not syncing' there; the false INCIDENT escalation was confined to the OAuth classifier).

expected_results: classify_mailbox_oauth_health maps conn_status=='REVOKED' to a new OWNER_DISCONNECTED status (SEV_OK, recovery_required=False, reconsent_required=False, 'No action' recommended action); conn_status=='ERROR' and the REAUTH_CODES remain RECONSENT_REQUIRED (the genuine owner-reconsent / 7-day-expiry case is preserved). A member's deliberate disconnect wins even over a leftover re-auth code and never escalates by age.

decide_alert treats OWNER_DISCONNECTED exactly like HEALTHY: never OPEN; RECOVER-once-then-clear if the mailbox was previously alerting. aggregate_oauth_health emits owner_disconnected_count and excludes member-revoked mailboxes from reconsent_required_count / any_recovery_required / worst_alert_severity / the operator_notice, while keeping them visible in counts_by_status and the per-mailbox list. The broker_mailbox_health CLI --oauth-health summary surfaces owner_disconnected (reconciling) and --exit-nonzero-on-reconsent no longer trips on a member disconnect.

core.operational_health.probe_mailbox_ingest never reports a FAULT (MISCONFIGURED/OFFLINE/BLOCKED/DEGRADED) for a benign member-revoked mailbox (OWNER_DISCONNECTED -> HealthState.HEALTHY). Value-blindness and every other ADR-0113 contract (owner-facing banner, dedup/cooldown/recovery, thresholds) are unchanged. Migration-free.

5-lens adversarial review (Workflow, 5 agents): correctness + security/value-blind CLEAN. Three LOW findings addressed: (downstream, CONFIRMED) the broker_mailbox_health CLI summary omitted owner_disconnected_count -> added + regression test; (scope/governance) ADR-0118 overclaimed 'the rest of the system treats REVOKED as benign' -> wording corrected (owner read-model deliberately differs; pre-existing R1 exit gates documented, not changed); (safety/false-negative, latent) the benign-disconnect invariant was only in ADR prose -> added a defensive comment at the ConnectedMailbox.Status.REVOKED enum. The review's alternative 'require no live REAUTH code' corroboration was considered and rejected because it regresses the realistic 'member disconnects a FAILING mailbox' case (MailboxRevokeView does not clear last_error_code); member intent remains authoritative, with the future-writer risk defended by the enum comment + ADR Consequences note.
limitations: Repository-only and DARK. The operator mailbox-health endpoint (BROKER_MAILBOX_OPERATOR_HEALTH_ENABLED) and the ingest/probe path (BROKER_INTELLIGENCE_INGEST_ENABLED) are the production arming gates; this change alters classification only and enables nothing. No production deploy, no flag enablement, no schedule.

The owner-facing banner (health.customer_mailbox_status / MailboxIngestionNotice) and the pre-pkt-149 R1 CLI exit gates (--exit-nonzero-on-recovery/-degraded, which read health.service_health where REVOKED maps to RECOVERY_REQUIRED) are intentionally NOT changed: an owner seeing 'reconnect to resume', and a monitor seeing 'a mailbox is not syncing', are both truthful. Only the OAuth operator-health INCIDENT escalation (reconsent/CRITICAL/MISCONFIGURED, and --exit-nonzero-on-reconsent) is corrected.

The benign classification rests on the VERIFIED invariant that status=REVOKED is member-initiated only (grepped: sole writer MailboxRevokeView; no code writes status=ERROR). This is defended by a code comment at the enum + an ADR Consequences note, not by a runtime guard (the value-blind classifier cannot see credential_ref, the only field that distinguishes a member disconnect from a hypothetical future grant-death-as-REVOKED).
